title: Proposal for More Severe Penalties for Scams Involving Impersonation of Government Agencies
what_it_is: Proposal for More Severe Penalties for Scams Involving Impersonation of Government Agencies

sections.label: Scam penalties and money mules
sections.summary: Existing penalties are assessed as adequate, with scammers and money mules facing up to 10 years' imprisonment, though many scammers are overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Our assessment is that the existing penalties are currently adequate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Depending on the facts of the case, scammers and money mules, including those involved in scams that impersonate government officials may face charges which carry imprisonment terms of up to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: However, many scammers are based overseas, making it difficult to identify and prosecute them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, in 2023, we amended the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act to allow the Police to take firmer enforcement action against money mules, whose bank accounts are used to perpetrate scams and other crimes.

sections.label: Recommended sentences for money mules
sections.summary: Recommended starting sentences are six months for negligent handing over of bank accounts and 18 months for knowing assistance to criminal proceeds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, the recommended starting sentence is six months' imprisonment for negligently handing over control of one's bank account to another person; and 18 months' imprisonment for handing over control of his bank account to another person, knowing or having reason to believe that this would assist the person in retaining criminal proceeds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs regularly reviews the adequacy of our criminal penalties and will likewise do so for scams-related offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In line with established case law, the fact that an offender has committed an offence, whether it is out of financial need or in the hope of recouping his losses due to being a scam victim, in and of itself does not have any mitigating value, save in the most exceptional or extreme circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For example, if it is a government official impersonation scam victim, and he went and he did money mule-related work, thinking that he was truly authorised by a government official, and he was deceived as to the nature of the money mule work that he was doing, then this would be taken into consideration by the courts.
